title: gridui-08: Drag a container between chrome regions — DnD hooks + the plugin escape hatch
summary: The drag framework ships but only the left sidebar is a drag surface. Regions and DockFrame have no hooks, so a container cannot be moved between regions.
description:
gridui-xx: Drag is a widget capability, not a region.

── Findings (verified in code 2026-10-19) ──
The structural refactor is DONE: T318 (delete the region layer / DragSurfaceId — gone from both crates) and T396 (framework-owned drag ghost + insertion line — SurfaceDragState/ghost_label gone from the app; the framework owns DragStart/Drag/DragEnd + DragEnter/Over/Leave/Drop with a computed side).
What remains (T325 DockFrame grip, T326 ChromeRegion/gaps accept a drop, T333 the move action) is "wire the dock drag," and it is BLOCKED on the move ACTION (T333) which does not exist yet. T325/T326 depend on T333. Shares its action-first shape with P030 (workspace reorder) — do them together. (T330 rejected.)

tasks.title: Drag is a widget capability, not a region: delete DragSurfaceId and the per-surface machinery
tasks.description:
**⚠️ This REVERSES the phase's "ADDITIVE ONLY — add variants, never remove one" rule, and the
original plan of this task ("add right sidebar, top bar and bottom bar variants"). Decided by
Antonio 2026-08-06, after F004/P084/T394 gave the framework a real drag vocabulary.**

His words: *"DND it's not only a thing of left/right/top/bottom bars? it should be available as
other widgets for plugin developers to be used in pane, overlay, sidebar, etc.. WHY WE ARE ALWAYS
HARDCODING?"* — and, about `heca/src/mouse/drag.rs`: *"this should be up to the DockView that
manages the workspaces, not the sidebar or the mouse."*

# Why the old plan is dead

Adding variants makes the enum longer, not open. A closed enum of **regions** cannot describe a
drag inside a pane, inside an overlay, or inside a plugin's own subtree — and a plugin cannot add a
variant at runtime, which is what T330 was invented to paper over.

The reason it looked like a region problem is historical: the app's drag predates the framework
having any, so it was built where the mouse events were, one handler per surface.

# What exists now (F004/P084/T394, 2026-08-06)

- `Base::drag_source` / `Base::drop_target` — universal, on **every** widget, declared with
  `DragExt::draggable(id)` / `.drop_target(id)`.
- The router emits `DragStart` / `Drag` / `DragEnd` / `DragEnter` / `DragOver` / `DragLeave` /
  `Drop` to whichever widget is under the pointer, with `DragEvent::side` (Before/Onto/After)
  already computed. It hit-tests **every mounted tree**, so this works in a pane, an overlay,
  either sidebar or a plugin subtree today — nothing in it names a region.
- 8 px threshold, capture, and the end-of-gesture guarantee (`DragEnd` always fires) are the
  framework's.

# The work

1. **Delete the region layer**: `DragSurfaceId`, `DragContext`, `SurfaceDragState`,
   `heca/src/mouse/drag.rs`, `heca/src/mouse/surface_left.rs`, `heca/src/mouse/target.rs`, the drag
   half of `heca/src/mouse/release.rs`, and `sidebar_bounds`. Also the early return at
   `heca/src/mouse.rs` (`if point_in_right_sidebar(...) { ...; return None; }`) — the reason the
   right sidebar could not drag at all while the left one could, with identical widgets.
2. **The ghost and the insertion line move INTO `heca-grid-ui`.** The app paints both per surface
   today; they are one drag visual for every drag, and a plugin cannot draw them. This is the only
   part that moves rather than being deleted.
3. **The workspace drop logic moves to `heca/src/providers/workspaces/`** — beside the rows it is
   about. The container declares its rows draggable, answers `Drop` with an action through the
   registry, and nothing named `surface_left.rs` exists.
4. `DragItemKind` — decide whether it survives at all; the payload is the host's, keyed by the
   opaque `DragItemId` the container itself registered.
5. T330 (plugin open variants) **dissolves** if this lands: there is no enum left to open.

# Done when

- A widget is draggable by declaring one id, wherever it is mounted.
- The right sidebar drags because nothing distinguishes it from the left.
- The move is still reachable from keyboard and RPC (the phase's action-first rule stands).
- Antonio drags in the app: left sidebar, right sidebar, and between them.

tasks.description:

The same move MUST be reachable by keyboard and RPC (input parity, AGENTS.md). A drag that does something no keybinding can do is a rule violation.

PREREQUISITE for the rest of P079: T325 (DockFrame grip) and T326 (ChromeRegion/gaps accept a drop) both depend on this action existing. Shares its shape with P030 (workspace drag-to-reorder): build both moves as actions first, then the drag is only the mouse surface.

tasks.title: The drag ghost and the insertion line belong to the framework, not to each surface
tasks.description:
Split out of `P079(F004)/T318` (which deletes the region layer) because this is the one part that
**moves into `heca-grid-ui`** rather than being deleted. Decided with T318, 2026-08-06.

# What exists

- **App-side, per surface.** `SurfaceDragState.ghost_label: Option<DragLabel>` carries the chip's
  text and a hand-maintained `x`/`y` (`heca/src/mouse/drag.rs` sets it on threshold and moves it on
  every cursor step); `heca/src/app/render.rs` paints it. The insertion indicator is drawn from
  `DropHit { bounds, side }` at the app's own call sites.
- `DragLabel` and `DropSide`/`DropHit` already live in `heca-grid-ui/src/drag/`, so the *types* are
  in the right crate; only the drawing and the position bookkeeping are not.
- Since F004/P084/T394 the framework owns the gesture: `DragStart`/`Drag`/`DragEnd` on the source,
  `DragEnter`/`DragOver`/`DragLeave`/`Drop` on the target, with `DragEvent::side` computed for it.

# Why it moves

A plugin's widget can be draggable (it declares one id) but **cannot draw the drag**: the ghost and
the insertion line are painted by app code that knows which sidebar it is in. One drag should look
like one drag wherever it happens, and the widget author should write none of it — the same bargain
as `Base::hovered` and the focus ring.

# The work

1. A framework-owned overlay for the in-flight drag: the ghost follows the pointer (the router
   already has every move), and the insertion line draws against the current drop target's bounds
   and `side`. Both painted through `PaintCx::with_overlay`, so they composite above everything, and
   both read every colour/radius/width from the `Theme` — no magic numbers, per the widget rules.
2. What the ghost *shows* is the widget's to say, not the framework's: reuse
   `Component::text_summary()` (the accessible-name path) for the default, with an explicit
   override for a source that wants something else. **Do not** re-introduce a host-supplied string
   that the app has to keep in step with the row it came from
   (`heca/src/mouse/drag.rs::drag_ghost_label` re-derives it from the session on every drag start).
3. Delete `SurfaceDragState.ghost_label` and its two writers, and the ghost paint in
   `heca/src/app/render.rs`.
4. Showcase: a drag demo that is not a sidebar — two lists in a panel — so the "works anywhere"
   claim is visible and not just asserted.
5. Docs: `docs/widgets.md` drag section + rustdoc, per the mandatory both-audiences rule.

# Edge cases

- A drag that ends over nothing still clears the ghost (`DragEnd` always fires — the framework
  guarantees it).
- The pointer leaving the window mid-drag (`Event::pointer_cancelled()`) clears both visuals.
- A source removed mid-drag (a rebuild during the gesture) must not leave a ghost painted.

# Done when

Antonio drags a row in the app and sees the same ghost and the same insertion line in the left
sidebar, the right sidebar, and a non-sidebar surface — with no app code drawing any of it.

tasks.title: Docks keep the order the user gives them; every dock has a header with grip, fold and resize (PR #356)
tasks.description:
Recorded after the fact, on Antonio's word (2026-11-23). PR #356, merged 2026-11-23 (merge 2fc3e2a0), made by the heca-pro session while testing heca-pro's rooms dock; no task existed for it.

WHAT IT DID
1. A dock moved by the user (drag, key or script) stays where it was put. Before, a dock carrying an `order` from `[[docks]]` was sorted back over the user's move (heca/src/chrome/docks/host/placing.rs, mounted.rs, host/mod.rs; tests in host/tests.rs and chrome/window/scene/tests/regions.rs).
2. Every dock has a header: grip, name and fold caret, drawn on RowVariant::Filled (heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/dock_frame.rs).
   - The grip carries the dock with no modifier key; the move key still carries it from anywhere.
   - `chrome.container.toggle_collapsed` and `chrome.container.resize` take an optional `container_id` (unset = the focused dock); `by` moves an edge the way pane resize does (heca/src/actions/builtins/chrome.rs, heca/src/input/build/chrome.rs, heca/src/input/action.rs, heca/src/handlers/docks/mod.rs, heca/src/app/interaction/policy.rs, heca/src/app/registry/).
   - The edge between two docks is a Splitter.
   - The header is the row above a dock's first row for k/h/l/j, handled once in heca/src/providers/actions.rs for every dock.
   - New library pieces: `DragExt::accepts_when` (a drop target takes only some sources — heca-grid-ui/src/builders/drag.rs, drag/resolve.rs, pointer/drag.rs), `DockFrame::title_size(WidgetSize)` (also in the SDK, heca-view/src/build/containers.rs), `DockFrame::GRIP` (the one reorder glyph).
   - The workspaces dock binds Alt+j/k in its `[[keys.surface]]` entry (keybindings.default.toml).
Docs: docs/widgets.md (DockFrame builders), docs/keybindings.md.

WHY HERE
P079 is "drag a container between chrome regions"; this finishes the user-facing side of moving and sizing docks (grip, order kept, resize), next to P030's workspace reorder.
